## Overview

LRPLF106 is the registered **response-link companion** to [LRPLF06](../lrp-rli-lf-006/index.qmd) (#584 decision 2). Same children, same adjustment set, same arm-gap parameterisation and the same randomised contrast `d_grp_time[t2]`; the single difference is the score mean.

Phoneme blending has ten **three-alternative forced-choice** items, so a child answering at random scores about 3.3 out of 10. The ordinary Beta-Binomial inverse-logit mean does not know that, and the LRPLF06 posterior uses the room it leaves: 24 of 215 fitted rows have posterior-mean expected proportions below one third, and at timepoint 2 it is 8 of 54 rows and 16% of the posterior mass. This companion constrains the mean to $\tfrac{1}{3} + \tfrac{2}{3}\,\operatorname{expit}(\eta_t)$, so its expected score cannot fall below the guessing level. Individual predicted scores can still fall below it.

**The two fits are one piece of evidence.** Because the links can disagree about the size of the effect, neither is sufficient on its own: both plans are marked link-sensitivity-required and the release gate refuses to publish either without the other.

_Causal labelling + level-model crossover caveat._ Every non-randomised coefficient is an **adjusted association** under the revised DAG (`dag/dag-language-reading.dagitty`, revised 2026-07-10). Measured skill parents are **deliberately excluded** as post-treatment mediators of the group×time effect; only the revised-DAG confounders hearing (HS = `hs`), speech (SP = `deapp_c`) and phonological memory (RW = `erbto`) — each with a missing-indicator — enter as adjusters. The group effect is `group x time`, parameterised as the covariate-adjusted arm gap at t1 (`arm_gap_t1`, a pre-randomisation *balance* quantity, never an effect) plus the change in that gap at each later wave (`d_grp_time[t]`; #552): after t2 the waitlist crosses over, so the **clean randomised contrast lives only at t2** — the t2 change `d_grp_time[t2]`, a difference-in-differences of adjusted levels, labelled *causal*; the t3/t4 changes are randomised early-start-versus-delayed-start schedule contrasts, not treated-versus-untreated effects, and the per-wave gaps `b_grp_time[t] = arm_gap_t1 + d_grp_time[t]` are kept as a derived levels view. SES excluded (non-DAG / redundant).

## Model

Beta-Binomial$(N, \mu\kappa, (1-\mu)\kappa)$ on the level count, $N = 10$, with the **guessing-floor score mean** $\mu_t = \tfrac{1}{3} + \tfrac{2}{3}\operatorname{expit}(\eta_t)$ and
$\eta_{t} = \alpha + \alpha_{\text{time}[t]} + b_{\text{grp}[t]}\text{group} + \gamma_A A_{\text{std},t} + g_{\text{ability}[t]}z(\text{blocks}) + \gamma_{\text{grp\_ability}}\,\text{group}\,z(\text{blocks}) + \sum_{c}\gamma_c\,z(c) + u_{\text{child}}$, where the $z(c)$ are the standardised revised-DAG confounders hearing (HS = `hs`), speech (SP = `deapp_c`) and phonological memory (RW = `erbto`), each with a missing-indicator; measured skill parents are excluded as post-treatment mediators.

![Model diagram](model_graph.png){#fig-model .lightbox fig-align="left"}

**Intercept anchor under the floor link.** The empirical-Bayes anchor is mapped back through the link before it is used as a linear-predictor location: the pooled pre-randomisation t1 proportion is 0.49, whose ordinary logit is −0.03 but whose guessing-floor value is −1.16. Anchoring on the raw logit would put the intercept prior about 1.1 logits from where this model needs it.
